prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1327; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Reports a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection on a weekday morning. Both vehicles driven at low speed prior to impact. Claimant states she felt neck and lower back discomfort at the scene but declined EMS transport. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Photos requested and vehicle inspection scheduled.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. She reports a back strain with stiffness and pain rated moderate, aggravated by sitting for long periods. She has seen her primary care provider and is following a home stretching routine. No prior back claims reported. Confirmed she has not contacted a lawyer and is handling the claim directly. Explained the process for medical bill submission and rental coverage.

Entry 3: Reviewed the damage estimate and scene photos. Front bumper cover, hood, and both headlamp assemblies show damage consistent with the reported low-speed impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle. Telematics data from the other driver's vehicle is inconsistent with a high-speed event. Physical damage liability appears clear and is being evaluated against the other carrier's coverage.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant regarding her medical records request. She provided authorization for release of records from her provider. Physical therapy referral noted in the chart. Claimant asked about the timeline for a settlement decision and was advised that a final evaluation will follow receipt of treatment records and medical bills. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks.

Entry 5: Received treatment notes showing a diagnosis of lumbar strain with a recommended course of physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medication. Records are consistent with the reported mechanism of injury and the claimant's description of symptoms. Bodily injury evaluation in progress. Claimant has been informed of the next steps and remains cooperative. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect current medical information.
